extracted.intended_audience: practitioners and parties in PTAB post‑grant proceedings (patent owners, petitioners, patent counsel), and PTAB staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for filing, opposing, and adjudicating motions to amend (including motions to amend under the MTA pilot program) in AIA post‑grant proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Covers timing, content, burden allocation, preliminary guidance, revised motions, Board discretion, and use of Office prior art searches/examination assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of MTA pilot options (preliminary guidance and revised MTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office proposes to formalize the two options in the MTA pilot program: (1) requesting preliminary guidance and (2) filing, without pre-authorization, a revised MTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options were part of the pilot and are to be implemented as formal rule provisions. The Office notes high utilization (at least 88% elected one or both options) and that these options are generally effective in prompting revisions to MTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original motion to amend: conferral and due date
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file one original motion to amend a patent, but only after conferring with the Board. Unless a due date is provided in a Board order, an original motion to amend must be filed no later than the filing of a patent owner response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner wants preliminary guidance, the request for preliminary guidance must be included in the original motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: when a motion to amend may be denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend may be denied where: (i) The amendment does not respond to a ground of unpatentability involved in the trial; or (ii) The amendment seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to amend must be responsive to the instituted grounds and cannot broaden claims or add new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable number of substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend may cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims. The presumption is that only one substitute claim will be needed to replace each challenged claim, and it may be rebutted by a demonstration of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should generally present one substitute per challenged claim unless they can demonstrate why more are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for any motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend claims must include a claim listing, which claim listing may be contained in an appendix to the motion, show the changes clearly, and set forth: (1) The support in the original disclosure of the patent for each proposed substitute claim; and (2) The support in an earlier-filed disclosure for each claim for which the benefit of the filing date of the earlier-filed disclosure is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must explicitly identify claim changes and show written‑description/support and any priority/benefit support; failure to do so risks denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motions to amend: authorization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for revised motions (see paragraph (f)), any additional motion to amend may not be filed without Board authorization. An additional motion to amend may be authorized when there is a good cause showing or a joint request of the petitioner and the patent owner to materially advance a settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will consider whether a petitioner submitted supplemental information after the motion-to-amend filing window when deciding to authorize additional motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner's burden of persuasion on motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner bears the burden of persuasion to show, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the motion to amend complies with the requirements of paragraphs (1) and (3) of 35 U.S.C. 316(d) (or 326(d) for PGR), as well as paragraphs (a)(2) and (3) and (b)(1) and (2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners must affirmatively demonstrate statutory/regulatory compliance (e.g., no new matter, responsive to ground) by a preponderance of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's burden of persuasion on proposed substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner bears the burden of persuasion to show, by a preponderance of the evidence, that any proposed substitute claims are unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must establish unpatentability of substitute claims by the preponderance standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to grant/deny motions and to raise new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrespective of the parties' burdens, the Board may exercise its discretion to grant or deny a motion to amend or raise a new ground of unpatentability in connection with a proposed substitute claim. Where the Board exercises its discretion to raise a new ground, the parties will have notice and an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's discretionary authority is broad and includes sua sponte raising of grounds; parties will be afforded notice and response opportunity when this occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may consider all evidence of record and related evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In exercising discretion under motions to amend, the Board may consider all evidence of record in the proceeding. The Board also may consider and make of record: (i) Any evidence in a related proceeding before the Office and evidence that a district court can judicially notice; and (ii) When no petitioner opposes or all petitioners cease to oppose a motion to amend, prior art identified through a prior art search conducted by the Office at the Board's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule broadens the record the Board may rely upon beyond the adversarially submitted materials, and permits inclusion of related-proceeding evidence and Office-conducted search results (when no opposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unpatentability on Board-raised grounds: standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board exercises its discretion to raise a new ground, the Board must determine unpatentability based on a preponderance of the evidence of record or made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when the Board raises a ground sua sponte or relies on evidence beyond petitioners' submissions, the preponderance standard applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary guidance: request, scope, and non‑binding nature
rubrics_metrics.description: In its original motion to amend, a patent owner may request that the Board provide preliminary guidance setting forth the Board's initial, preliminary views on the original motion to amend, including whether the parties have shown a reasonable likelihood of meeting their respective burdens and notice of any new ground discretionarily raised by the Board. Any preliminary guidance will not be binding on the Board, is not a 'decision' under § 42.71(d), and is not a final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary guidance is an initial, advisory view intended to aid patent owners in deciding whether/how to revise; it can trigger timing consequences but cannot be appealed as a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies and sur‑replies following preliminary guidance: limits on new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to preliminary guidance, a patent owner may file a reply to the petitioner's opposition, the preliminary guidance (if no opposition is filed), or a revised motion to amend; the reply or revised motion may be accompanied by new evidence. If a patent owner does not file either a reply or a revised motion, the petitioner may file a reply to the preliminary guidance, but such a reply may only respond to the preliminary guidance and may not be accompanied by new evidence. If the petitioner files such a reply, a patent owner may file a sur-reply, but that sur-reply may only respond to the petitioner's reply and may not be accompanied by new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence may accompany patent-owner replies or revised MTAs, but petitioners' replies to preliminary guidance and subsequent patent-owner sur-replies are limited to responsive argument only (no new evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised motion to amend: one without prior authorization and replacement effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may, without prior authorization from the Board, file one revised motion to amend after receiving an opposition to the original motion to amend or after receiving the Board's preliminary guidance. A revised motion to amend must be responsive to issues raised in the preliminary guidance or in the petitioner's opposition and must include one or more new proposed substitute claims (each presenting a new claim amendment). If a patent owner files a revised motion to amend, that revised motion replaces the original motion to amend in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised motion is the sole non‑authorized additional amendment vehicle and must address the Board's or petitioner's raised issues; it supplants the original motion when filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may solicit examination assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has discretion to solicit examination assistance if the petitioner ceases to participate altogether or if the petitioner does not oppose or ceases to oppose an MTA. Examination assistance could include an advisory report on whether an MTA meets certain statutory and regulatory requirements (e.g., enlarges scope or introduces new matter) and the patentability of proposed substitute claims in light of prior art provided by the patent owner and/or obtained by examiner searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soliciting exam assistance is a mechanism to obtain Office expertise on statutory/regulatory compliance and patentability when adversarial participation is lacking or limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office prior art search at Board request and making results of record
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule confirms that the Board may request a prior art search by the Office when no petitioner opposes or all petitioners cease to oppose an MTA. The Board may make of record any evidence identified through a prior art search undertaken at the Board's request. The Board's request and the prior art search report prepared by the Office at the request of the Board will be made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no opposition exists, the Office-conducted search and report become part of the proceeding record and may be considered by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of MTA timelines and final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: To address concerns about sufficient time, the Board may extend deadlines in the MTA timeline for good cause. The AIA authorizes the Director (delegated to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge) to extend the deadline for issuing a final written decision for good cause and by not more than 6 months (beyond the one-year statutory deadline). Panels typically determine whether to grant good-cause extensions after request and conference with the parties under 37 CFR 42.5(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary and reserved for situations like complex issues, panel unavailability, need to accommodate additional briefing or evaluation of an Office search report, compressed schedules due to revised MTAs, or multiple hearing postponements (cases cited: Eden Park, Hope Medical, Snap). Parties should request and confer when seeking extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Board consideration of broader record alleviates prior limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule removes limitations such as requiring consideration only of 'readily identifiable and persuasive' evidence or relying solely on the adversarial system, thereby allowing the Board to consider the entirety of the art of record and request examination assistance when justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change responds to judicial concerns (e.g., Hunting Titan decision criticized) and expands the kinds of evidence the Board may rely upon in evaluating amended claims and raising grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary guidance may trigger extension determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may, upon issuing preliminary guidance, for good cause and on a case-by-case basis, determine whether to extend the final written decision more than one year from the date a trial is instituted and whether to extend any remaining deadlines under § 42.5(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance of preliminary guidance is explicitly tied to possible timeline adjustments, recognizing that addressing guidance (e.g., obtaining expert testimony, searching for art) may require additional time.
